changed_invariants: P15 owns an explicit quantized affine local clock with microsecond and ppm units.
PPS sequence identity, rather than received array position, determines the synthetic reference epoch.
A strict inter-PPS gap timeout captures at equality before evaluating lateness.
Timestamp flooring uses an eight-quotient-ULP affine-operation bound; positive timeout equality uses one gap-scale ULP and zero timeout has no tolerance.
Absolute timestamp tick indices are limited to 1e12 so the eight-ULP boundary guard cannot become upward rounding over a material fraction of one tick.
PPS gaps derive from sequence-ID deltas times period instead of subtracting absolute epochs.
Cancellation retains the pre-timeout PPS prefix, censors later anchors, and never changes raw timestamps.
The public lesson owns one interactive launch; experiment.m no longer creates a duplicate UI and callback lifetime.
P15 permanent tests do not freeze the moving implementation frontier.
residual_risks: No MATLAB runtime or rendered UI execution was available.
An ideal affine clock and deterministic floor quantization do not model oscillator wander, capture latency, leap seconds, receiver faults, or timestamp provenance.
Within the 1e12 tick-index ceiling, eight-ULP tick and one-ULP positive-timeout boundary policies are floating-point representation guards, not evidence for a fixed-point hardware timestamp counter.
Educational effectiveness requires a learner session and teach-back.
